newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban militia capture Kabul - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Taleban militia capture Kabul - witnesses.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic militia entered Kabul in tanks and on foot overnight on Friday, meeting little resistance from forces loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani, witnesses said.

Celebratory bursts of machine-gun fire and occasional explosions echoed across the city at dawn but the Afghan capital was relatively calm as Taleban fighters set up checkpoints to search vehicles, the eyewitnesses said.

Earlier, Taleban sources in Pakistan had said the Islamic militia appeared poised to capture the capital after seizing the main government airbase north of Kabul and parts of the city, including its abandoned Khwaja Rawash airport.

Deputy foreign minister Adbul Rahim Ghafoorzai told Reuters Television at the United Nations late on Thursday that government troops were leaving Kabul to avoid a "bloodbath" with the rebels, and the country's besieged president was considering handing over power.
The minister said that the country's military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, had gone north of the city, taking with him jet fighters and other military hardware.
